themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 74 this week versus 16.5 weekly average—a 348% increase (z-score: 7.17)—suggesting rapid pavement, pothole, or sidewalk degradation across CD 314 demanding immediate infrastructure assessment.
evidence: 74 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 16.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (348% spike, z-score 7.17)
Root/Sewer/Sidewalk condition complaints also elevated: 4 last week vs. 1.2 weekly average (220% spike, z-score 6.35)
Street sign damage spike: 5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (1233% spike, z-score 6.65)
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: photograph and map the worst street/sidewalk damage clusters in Midwood and Ocean Parkway corridors
Departmental accountability: query DOT on response times and maintenance budget allocation to CD 314 versus other districts

themes_detail.label: Water System & Plumbing Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints jumped to 54 this week from 17.9 weekly average—a 202% spike (z-score: 5.57)—concurrent with 772 cumulative plumbing complaints suggesting possible main breaks, contamination, or pressure loss affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: Water system complaints THIS WEEK: 54 vs. 17.9 weekly average (202% spike, z-score 5.57)
Plumbing complaints cumulative (90 days): 772 total—among top 10 complaint types district-wide
Heat/hot water complaints dominant category (6088 over 90 days)—may indicate water delivery/pressure issues
reporting_angles: Call DEP: have there been main breaks, water main flushing, or pressure issues reported in Midwood/Ocean Parkway this week?
Resident interviews: identify blocks with recurring water shutoffs or low-pressure conditions; visual confirmation of street excavation or repairs

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Double in One Week
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 47 this week versus 12.5 weekly average—a 276% increase (z-score: 7.71)—suggesting new construction, events, or enforcement activity that warrants identification.
evidence: Street/Sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK: 47 vs. 12.5 weekly average (276% spike, z-score 7.71)
Residential noise also elevated at category level (1837 cumulative, top 3 complaint type)
DOB data shows 301 alteration permits filed in last 90 days—225 are active alterations, likely ongoing construction
reporting_angles: Construction audit: cross-reference noise spikes with DOB alteration permit locations; identify which sites are actively working this week without proper noise permits
Timeline correlation: determine if spike coincides with specific rezoning hearings (Ditmas Park West, Beverley Square West historic district reviews underway) or street work projects

themes_detail.label: Encampment Emergence & Homelessness Signal
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 4 this week from 0.2 weekly baseline—a 1500% spike (z-score: 5.67)—indicating rapid visible homelessness increase in CD 314, consistent with citywide trends but requiring on-ground verification and social services coordination.
evidence: Encampment complaints THIS WEEK: 4 vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score 5.67)
Real Time Enforcement complaints also elevated last week: 7 vs. 2.6 average (167% spike, z-score 5.11)—may reflect increased NYPD/enforcement activity in response
Concurrent noise and street condition spikes suggest areas of disorder/neglect clustering in specific microgeographies
reporting_angles: On-the-ground reporting: map the 4 encampment complaints geographically; visit sites to assess scale, conditions, and service availability
System story: interview HRA, NYPD, and local social services about resourcing for homeless outreach in Midwood given district's transit access and commercial corridors

themes_detail.label: Illegal Fireworks Complaints Vanish After Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints peaked at 6 three weeks ago (2300% above 0.2 weekly baseline, z-score: 13.28)—the highest severity spike in the dataset—but current status unclear; warrants follow-up to determine if July 4th anomaly, ongoing activity, or enforcement success.
evidence: Illegal fireworks complaints 3 weeks ago: 6 vs. 0.2 weekly average (2300% spike, highest z-score: 13.28 in entire dataset)
No subsequent weeks of data provided—unclear if spike was one-time July 4 event or sustained pattern
Noise complaints remain elevated THIS WEEK, but fireworks-specific complaints not mentioned in current spike list
reporting_angles: NYPD follow-up: obtain precinct-level arrest/summons data for illegal fireworks in CD 314 for June–July; determine if peak was holiday-driven
Resident survey: query NextDoor, community boards, or local social media for continued fireworks complaints to assess if trend persists below 311 threshold
